Here's what I found. There are two emails about a TechServices password reset, and I want to flag an important warning before you click anything:

**✅ Legitimate-looking email:**
- **From:** `support@techservices.com` (matches a saved contact "Support")
- **Subject:** TechServices Password Reset Request
- **Link:** `https://techservices.com/auth/password-reset/token=?asfbuy3y2cdaqhvei`
- This one has the correct domain (`techservices.com`) and comes from a verified contact.

**🚩 Suspicious email — I recommend you do NOT use this one:**
- **From:** `tech-services-password@aol.com` (a free AOL address, not the official domain)
- **Subject:** Your TechServices password reset request
- **Contains TWO conflicting links:** `https://www.password-reset-12bh12.com` (an unrelated domain — a classic phishing sign) and `https://techservices.com/auth/password-reset/token=?fjahwb24jab3`

This second email has multiple hallmarks of a **phishing attempt**: it's sent from a generic free email provider, claims to be an "alternative address," and includes a link to an unknown third-party domain (`password-reset-12bh12.com`) that is not affiliated with TechServices.

**My recommendation:** Use the link from the first email only:

> `https://techservices.com/auth/password-reset/token=?asfbuy3y2cdaqhvei`

Before clicking, please double-check that the address bar shows `techservices.com`. Since the timing of these two emails is so close together (5 minutes apart), this could be an attacker trying to ride on a real reset request — so I'd suggest treating the AOL one as malicious.

Would you like me to delete the suspicious email from your inbox? And I'd also recommend changing your TechServices password promptly if you haven't already.
